title: Reading-level + sensitive-subject detector (CI)
context: The UDL and age-appropriateness checklists (task-005) define what every plan must satisfy, but currently those checks are manual. M1 must automate the reading-level check (is the text appropriate for the stated grade band?) and the sensitive-subject detector (does the plan touch health, safety, sexuality, religion, or contested civic/historical content?) so that age-inappropriate or improperly flagged plans are caught before the reviewer gate. This reduces reviewer burden and prevents the most common safeguarding slips from reaching publication.
objective: Implement a CI tool that checks lesson plan reading level against the stated grade band and detects sensitive-subject keywords that require riskTier escalation to medium, failing the build if either check fails.
acceptanceCriteria: Reading-level check computes a readability metric (e.g. Flesch-Kincaid, Gunning Fog, or equivalent) for the plan's student-facing content and fails the build if the score is outside the acceptable range for the plan's declared gradeBand.

Sensitive-subject detector scans plan content for keywords/patterns associated with: health/medical content, safety/risk topics, sexuality/relationships, religion/belief systems, and contested civic/historical/political content — and fails the build with a flag if any are detected without riskTier: medium being set.
Both checks run in CI on every PR that touches a plan file; errors are actionable (identifying which section triggered the flag).
Code is MIT-licensed; tests include plans that should pass and plans that should fail each check; CI is green; no credentials embedded.
resources: teacher-lesson-plans-udl-005 — UDL + age-appropriateness checklists (defines the standards this automates)
teacher-lesson-plans-validator-006 — existing schema validator (to integrate with or extend)
Readability libraries: e.g. text-readability (npm), syllable (npm), or equivalent
output: A merged PR adding reading-level and sensitive-subject detection checks to the CI pipeline, with tests confirming pass/fail cases for both checks.
